# Data Masking reference scenarios

Generated by tools/reference/generate-datamasking.mjs using the installed public CommonJS DataMasking export from @aws-lambda-powertools/data-masking@2.35.0. No upstream code is patched.

The 240 scenarios compare complete erasure results, errors, warnings, provider plaintext/ciphertext arguments, authenticated context and result shapes. Coverage includes default collapse, array length preservation, nulls, custom empty masks, explicit false dynamic masks, UTF-16 mask length, nested leaves, dot/wildcard expressions, sequential/duplicate/overlapping field rules, rule precedence, reserved keys, missing-field policy, selected/full transforms and JSON key order. Both sides use an explicitly non-cryptographic deterministic provider. Provider calls are compared as complete multisets because Go starts operations concurrently; other recorded output and warning order remains exact.

These cases do not prove encryption security, ciphertext interoperability, KMS integration, cache behavior, built-in JavaScript RegExp replacement, arbitrary JavaScript prototypes/cyclic cloning, native serialization or exhaustive number/Unicode diagnostics. The Go tests separately cover 64 concurrent erasures, input snapshots, cancellation, replacement errors, concurrent provider operations, authenticated-context ownership, provider error identity and caller-side panic propagation.

An additional recorded async-failure timeline proves that the first rejected operation is observed before an unrelated pending provider completes. A native blocking-provider test verifies the same return-before-release behavior while preserving the first error identity.
